Based on your 9 pages, **the BLUETTI AC200L is my top recommendation** for an RV owner who wants approximately 2kWh of capacity, a built-in 30A RV outlet, and a price under $900.

<AsyncImageGroup query={["BLUETTI AC200L portable power station front view TT-30 RV outlet","BLUETTI AC200L portable power station RV camping setup"]} aspectRatio="5:4" layout="bento"/>

<text color="success" weight="medium" size="sm">BEST OVERALL FOR RV USE</text>

**BLUETTI AC200L**

| Specification | Details |
|---|---|

| RV outlet | Built-in TT-30 |

Source: [DealElectric's 2026 comparison](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv)

## Important: What can a 2kWh station actually run in your RV?

A built-in TT-30 outlet does **not** mean you get the full 30A (3,600W) of campground power.

According to your DealElectric comparison:

| Appliance | Practical expectation |
|---|---|
| RV refrigerator | Yes |
| Lights, fans, water pump | Yes |
| Coffee maker | Generally yes |
| Microwave | Yes, but watch simultaneous loads |
| Microwave + electric kettle | May overload |
| Rooftop air conditioner | Generally not practical for sustained use |

A typical rooftop AC may require 1,300–1,900W to run and substantial surge power to start. That can drain a 2kWh station very quickly.

Also, remember to turn off your RV's converter/charger when the house battery is fully charged, and set a two-way refrigerator to propane mode where available.

Source: [DealElectric — RV power limitations](https://dealectric.com/best-2kwh-power-station-for-rv)

## My final verdict

- **Best overall:** BLUETTI AC200L — especially at $854.05 with the discount.
- **Best for portability:** Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 — significantly lighter.
- **Best lower-cost alternative:** Growatt INFINITY 2000 PRO — impressive value if the outlet configuration works for your RV.

One caveat: these prices were collected on October 30–31, 2026, and can change. Also, the AC200L is described as being late in its product lifecycle, so I'd confirm stock and warranty terms before ordering.

If I were buying specifically for an RV with a standard 30A shore-power cord, **I'd buy the BLUETTI AC200L at the discounted $854 price.**

judge.why: The answer recommends our BLUETTI AC200L using dealectric.com figures, but it never gives the runtime (about 1.5 days, or 2-3 days with solar) or the recharge options (solar, alternator, campground outlet) that the concern asks about.
judge.concern: How long a 2 kWh station lasts on an RV weekend: about 1.2-1.5 kWh a day (fridge, furnace blower, lights), so about a day and a half on its own and two to three days with 200-400 W of solar, and how to recharge it (solar, an alternator charger, a campground outlet).
